- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; increase forecast slightly above recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops; add small upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overestimates continuation; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or adjust downward 1–2 days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in medium-term (15–30d) horizons when sentiment is mixed or neutral; add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias if sentiment swings from negative to positive.
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., ±0.5+ in sentiment), model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend, especially if sentiment is trending upward.
- When sentiment is flat or near-zero, model often overfits short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average or median of recent 7–14d to anchor forecast.
